methods.label: Combine the conjugate denominators
methods.explanation:
The denominators \(1+\sqrt3\) and \(1-\sqrt3\) are both nonzero. They are conjugates, so their product simplifies by the difference-of-squares formula:
\[
(1-\sqrt3)(1+\sqrt3)=1-3=-2.
\]
Combine the fractional terms first. Their common-denominator numerator is
\[
(1+\sqrt3)-(1-\sqrt3)=2\sqrt3.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac1{1-\sqrt3}-\frac1{1+\sqrt3}
=\frac{2\sqrt3}{-2}=-\sqrt3.
\]
Adding the initial \(1\) gives \(1-\sqrt3\), choice A.
methods.levelReason: Uses a common denominator, the difference-of-squares identity and elementary radical arithmetic.
